key_insight: LLM agents can help reproduce published scientific findings and flag analytical choices that may affect conclusions for expert review.
engineering_relevance: Executable reproduction baselines and automated robustness checks offer a practical foundation for research-validation workflows.
method: Build SEER-Repro from 20 published cancer-registry studies and their reproduction resources.
Use an AI agent to reproduce atomic claims and generate executable baselines.
Identify analytical choices, propose defensible alternatives, and rerun analyses to test conclusion stability.
evidence_signal: The agent reproduced 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims; the robustness pipeline flagged potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings.
watch_item: Evaluation is limited to SEER-based studies, and flagged analytical choices require expert review rather than establishing that findings are invalid.
paper_title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
